rationale: The investigators retained 87 single-agent modafinil cases from a poison-center database. Two had hallucinations, and one clinical narrative explicitly describes visual hallucinations following a large unintended exposure. This measures adverse presentation after pharmaceutical exposure, without a Parkinson cohort or dried-fig contrast.

The principal case concerns toxic white-matter disease after exposure to a household chemical. The case includes gait impairment and cogwheel rigidity. Visual hallucinations and parkinsonism also appear in discussion of other toxic presentations. These passages address a differential diagnosis and supply no dried-fig contrast or confirmed Parkinson visual-event outcome.

The review reuses the sleep comparison of 14 left-onset and 17 right-onset Parkinson participants with 17 chronically ill controls from PMID 18797256. The studies of spatial perception and sleep use different tests. In Figure 12 the review reverses the sleep-item scale for frequency display. Nocturnal hallucination ratings are not a separately counted visual-episode outcome for dried figs.

The paper summarizes cortical Lewy body clinicopathology and describes work distinguishing presynaptic aggregates from conspicuous Lewy bodies. It reports mostly null correlations of broad body counts with clinical findings and cites regional temporal associations for formed visual hallucinations. Regional pathology, disease classification and episode frequency are distinct. No food intervention is described.

The study describes seven PLA2G6-associated cases with differing ages of onset. One adult case had transient visual hallucinations early in a progressive dystonia-parkinsonism syndrome and later had a cortical biopsy. The case description gives timing but no recurrence estimate. Its diagnosis, tissue findings and treatment history do not supply an idiopathic Parkinson food comparison.

The case series examines five families with complex early-onset parkinsonism and reuses previously reported clinical descriptions. Visual hallucinations appear in the background on earlier ATP13A2 follow-up. One FBXO7-family case developed psychosis during levodopa treatment, prompting clinicians to withdraw it. The authors give no visual episode count for this case or a dietary comparison.

RECOVER randomized 287 participants with Parkinson disease to the rotigotine patch or placebo. The distressing-hallucinations sleep item did not improve within the active group in the reported post hoc summary. A broader perception and hallucinations score and one serious visual-hallucination withdrawal are separate observations. The trial studied a patch and did not count visual episodes after dried-fig intake.

In five adults with a history of Dravet syndrome, motor slowness, hypomimia and perseveration resembled features seen in other disorders. One narrative describes recurring hallucinatory symptoms in adulthood and no indication of hallucinations during a later examination. The article does not classify those experiences by sensory modality or compare diagnosed Parkinson participants receiving dried figs.
